hypotheses.justification: The other hypotheses imply it. By [Nontrivial V] pick v ≠ 0. The K-span of {ρ g v | g : GL2 q} is a ρ-invariant subspace, so it is a Subrepresentation, and it is nonzero. By hirr it is ⊤. GL2 q = GL (Fin 2) (ZMod q) is finite, so this span is finitely generated, hence V is finite-dimensional. Build the instance locally and the existing proof (IsIrreducible, then Representation.char_orthonormal) goes through unchanged.

The identity holds in every characteristic. Let T : End V → End V, T(A) = ∑_g ρ(g) A ρ(g⁻¹). Each T(A) commutes with every ρ(h). V is irreducible (from hirr and Nontrivial V) and finite-dimensional, and K is algebraically closed, so by Schur's lemma T(A) = f(A)·id for a linear map f. A linear map of the form A ↦ f(A)·id has trace f(id), and T(id) = |G|·id, so tr T = |G| in K. Also, the trace of A ↦ X A Y on End V ≅ V ⊗ V* equals tr X · tr Y, so tr T = ∑_g χ(g) χ(g⁻¹). Hence ∑_g χ(g)χ(g⁻¹) = (Nat.card G : K) without any characteristic assumption; when char K divides |G| both sides are 0. The proof must replace char_orthonormal (which needs |G| invertible) with this Schur/trace argument.
